question: On 20 October 2026, the Lviv Regional Council declared 2027 to be the Year of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) and Roman Shukhevych. As commander of the UPA, Roman Shukhevych bore responsibility for the systematic murders of tens of thousands of Polish civilians in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia between 1943 and 1945, which Poland recognises as genocide.

Prior to this, he served in the Nachtigall Battalion, a unit that collaborated with the Germans. The official glorification of individuals associated with organisations responsible for the mass murder of civilians is contrary to the values of respect for human dignity and human rights enshrined in Article 2 TEU.

It also runs counter to the EU’s position on the rehabilitation of regimes and formations responsible for crimes against civilians. The instigator is Sviatoslav Sheremeta, Chair of Lviv Oblast Council’s Culture Committee and a public advocate for this decision. Will the Council consider imposing EU entry bans and other restrictive measures on those involved in this matter?
